wedge: public K-apt monthly apartment management-fee data + same-complex history + similar-complex benchmarks => consumer-facing monthly anomaly watch that flags what jumped, how unusual it is, and which category drove the change; generic lookup/comparison is explicitly excluded
last_material_result: Data-feasibility check PASSED, while competition risk strengthened. The official Public Data Portal exposes separate Ministry of Land K-apt OpenAPIs for common management fees, individual-use charges, long-term repair reserves, complex lists and basic information; these are free and the catalog shows substantial existing API usage, so automated public-data refresh is technically plausible without private resident data. However, K-apt itself already offers monthly fee lookup, map search, 1:1 and 1:N comparisons, regional averages and custom statistics, and a consumer site (aptdamoa.com) already combines K-apt fees with transaction/subscription data. Therefore wedge #2 move-in due-diligence comparison is weak and should not be pursued as a generic comparison report. The surviving differentiation is proactive anomaly detection / plain-language cause explanation, which official browse tools do not obviously foreground. No build yet.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Data acquisition can plausibly stay free via government OpenAPI. Direct consumer WTP remains weak; viable economics likely require organic apartment-name/search traffic plus ads/affiliate/lead-gen, or later premium alerts. Maintenance burden is moderate because monthly data refresh and anomaly rules can be automated, but monetization is not yet evidenced.
next_checkpoint: Next Lane C run: validate the remaining two action-layer wedges rather than generic comparison: (1) recurring 'this month's fee jumped' anomaly alert and (3) 'why did my fee jump?' category explainer. Look for repeated consumer-language demand and existing products that already send proactive fee anomaly alerts. If proactive demand/substitute gap is weak after both wedges, KILL the candidate and return to fresh discovery.
recommendation: KEEP in ASSESS for one more bounded demand/substitute test. Data feasibility is confirmed enough for validation; do not BUILD. Drop generic move-in comparison as a wedge because official and third-party substitutes are already strong.
